titleText.es: Historia real (de Randall Munroe): tuve que hacer varios intentos para subir esta tira porque mi clave SSH estaba en la lista negra.
titleText.en: True story (from Randall Munroe): I had to make several attempts to upload this strip because my SSH key was blacklisted.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive explicitly identifies Randall Munroe in parentheses; the official English title text begins simply with ‘True story.’ Both versions refer to an SSH key affected by the real Debian OpenSSL weak-key incident.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to comment out; to disable a line of code by marking it as a comment
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In programming, comentar can mean turning executable code into a comment so that the computer ignores it. This is more specific than ordinary comentar, ‘to comment on something.’

example.es: Voy a comentar esta línea mientras pruebo el programa.
example.en: I am going to comment out this line while I test the program.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: urgency; rush; urgent situation
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Urgencia can name either the need to act quickly or the urgent situation causing that pressure.

example.en: They fixed the fault urgently.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to; connects an urgency or rush to the action prompting it
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After a noun such as urgencia or prisa, por can introduce the action someone is eager or pressed to complete. Natural English often uses ‘to’ instead of translating por as ‘for.’

example.en: There was a rush to finish.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: fiasco; major embarrassing failure
cardDefinitions.noteEn: A fiasco is a conspicuous failure, especially one involving confusion, poor planning, or public embarrassment.

example.en: The launch was a fiasco.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: marks an action whose doer is not named
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Before a third-person verb, se can focus on what happens rather than who does it. English often uses a passive form such as ‘is requested’ or ‘have been discovered.’

example.en: Several errors were found.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: discovered; found (completed-action form used after haber)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Descubierto is the irregular completed-action form of descubrir. After a form of haber, it stays unchanged: he descubierto, han descubierto, and so on.

example.en: They have discovered a new error.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: series; set; succession
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Una serie de introduces a related group or succession of people, things, or events.

example.en: There was a series of problems.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; links a hole or problem to the field of security
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish uses de in compounds such as agujero de seguridad and problema de seguridad. English normally puts ‘security’ directly before the other noun.

example.en: They found a security problem.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: important; major (plural)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Importante has the same masculine and feminine singular form. The plural importantes ends in -es.

example.en: Several important matters remain.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: affected (masculine singular)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Afectado describes a masculine singular person or thing that experiences the effect of a problem or event.

example.en: The affected system is disconnected.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: vulnerable; open to harm or attack
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Vulnerable has the same form for masculine and feminine singular nouns. Use vulnerable a before the danger or influence involved.

example.es: El servidor es vulnerable a ese ataque.
example.en: The server is vulnerable to that attack.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to; introduces the danger after vulnerable
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The adjective vulnerable normally takes a before the attack, influence, or problem that can cause harm.

example.es: La planta es vulnerable al frío.
example.en: The plant is vulnerable to the cold.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: cipher; encryption; encoded form
cardDefinitions.noteEn: As a noun, cifrado can name a method or system for encoding information. The verb cifrar means ‘to encrypt’ or ‘to encode.’

example.es: Este cifrado es fácil de romper.
example.en: This cipher is easy to break.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: gives; grants
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Da is the present form of dar used with one other person or thing. In technical contexts, dar acceso means ‘to grant access.’

example.es: La tarjeta da acceso al edificio.
example.en: The card grants access to the building.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: access; entry; permission to use something
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Acceso can refer to physical entry or permission to use a system, account, or resource.

example.es: No tengo acceso a esa cuenta.
example.en: I do not have access to that account.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: is asked; is requested (with se)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pide is the present form of pedir used with one other person or thing. With passive se, se pide focuses on what is requested rather than who requests it.

example.en: A password is requested.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: flattery
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Adulación is exaggerated praise used to please or influence someone.

example.es: No se dejó convencer por la adulación.
example.en: He was not persuaded by flattery.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: belonging to; often expressed with ’s in English
cardDefinitions.noteEn: De can connect a thing to its owner. Spanish says el libro de Ana where English can say ‘Ana’s book.’

example.en: It is Luis's computer.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: user (masculine singular or generic)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Usuario is a person who uses a service, device, or computer account. The feminine form is usuaria.

example.en: Each user has a password.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: friend (masculine singular)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Amigo can identify a male friend or appear as the masculine dictionary form when discussing the word itself.

example.en: Pablo is a good friend.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: Elvish; relating to elves or an elf language
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Élfico can describe something associated with fantasy elves. Used after en, it can name an Elvish language.

example.es: La inscripción está escrita en élfico.
example.en: The inscription is written in Elvish.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: it turns out
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Resulta que introduces information that has just been discovered, is surprising, or changes the listener's understanding.

example.es: Resulta que la tienda está cerrada.
example.en: It turns out that the store is closed.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: that; introduces what turns out to be true
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After resulta, que opens the newly revealed statement. Learn resulta que together as ‘it turns out that.’

example.en: It turns out that you were right.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: software distribution; distro
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Distro is informal technical shorthand for distribución, especially a packaged version of an operating system such as a Linux distribution.

example.es: Probé una distro diferente de Linux.
example.en: I tried a different Linux distribution.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: several; various (masculine plural)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Varios before a plural noun means more than one, usually an unspecified small number or range.

example.en: We tried several designs.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: themes; visual appearance packages
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In software, a tema is a coordinated set of colors, images, and styles that changes how an interface looks. In other contexts, tema can mean ‘topic.’

example.es: La aplicación incluye varios temas oscuros.
example.en: The application includes several dark themes.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: custom; customized (masculine plural)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Personalizados describes masculine plural things adapted to a particular person, purpose, or preference.

example.en: We sell custom designs.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: firm; stern (describing a voice)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: When firme describes a voice or tone, it means controlled, confident, and not yielding. This is different from merely saying that a hand or object does not shake.

example.en: She answered in a firm voice.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: se + verbo en tercera persona (sin nombrar quién actúa)
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can Spanish focus on an action or result without naming who does it?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Put se before a third-person verb and state what happens; the person doing it can remain unnamed.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: English often uses a passive form. Spanish may use se with a simple verb or with a completed construction such as se han encontrado. Other uses of se follow different patterns.

example.en: The results were published.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you name a weakness that can be exploited in a system?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Say agujero de seguridad; use agujeros de seguridad for more than one.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The expression literally uses ‘hole of security,’ while natural English puts the field first: ‘security hole.’ Vulnerabilidad de seguridad is another common technical term.

example.es: El parche corrige un agujero de seguridad.
example.en: The patch fixes a security hole.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say what danger or influence something is vulnerable to?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use vulnerable a before the danger; a and el combine as al.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The describing word vulnerable stays the same in masculine and feminine singular. Its complement begins with a, even when English uses ‘to.’

example.es: Este material es vulnerable al agua.
example.en: This material is vulnerable to water.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something grants or provides access?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of dar followed by acceso; use a before the place, system, or resource when it is stated.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The form of dar changes with the subject: da acceso, dan acceso, dio acceso, and so on.

example.es: La llave da acceso al almacén.
example.en: The key grants access to the warehouse.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you introduce a surprising fact that has just become clear?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use resulta que, then state the newly revealed information.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Resulta que often corresponds to ‘it turns out that.’ It frames the next statement as a discovery or correction to what someone expected.

example.en: It turns out that they already knew each other.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: fiasco de Debian-OpenSSL · agujeros de seguridad · sistemas vulnerables
cardDefinitions.answerEn: the comic turns a real Debian OpenSSL weak-key incident into a list of absurd security flaws in other operating systems
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Debian's 2008 OpenSSL vulnerability made cryptographic keys predictable and affected SSH keys, matching the title text about a blacklisted key. The left panels joke that essential safeguards were commented out; the table then invents vulnerabilities based on stereotypes, fantasy references, and software reputations.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: a simple substitution cipher that shifts every letter by the same fixed number of positions
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The method is associated with Julius Caesar. Because there are very few possible shifts, it is easy to test every key; calling a modern operating system vulnerable to it is intentionally absurd.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: a reference to Independence Day, where Jeff Goldblum's character uses a PowerBook to help upload a virus to the alien mothership
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The comic turns that film scene into a mock software vulnerability: merely encountering the named laptop supposedly threatens the operating system.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: a reference to the Doors of Durin in The Lord of the Rings, opened by saying mellon, the Elvish word for “friend”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The comic reimagines the fantasy door's spoken solution as a laughably weak computer-access rule.

regions.labelEs: DURANTE LA URGENCIA POR ARREGLAR EL FIASCO DE DEBIAN-OPENSSL, SE HAN DESCUBIERTO UNA SERIE DE AGUJEROS DE SEGURIDAD IMPORTANTES:

excludedUnits.rationale: Debian and OpenSSL are unchanged software-project names joined in the printed incident label, not Spanish lexical words.

applications.explanationEn: Han supplies the present form of haber for a plural reference, and descubierto is descubrir's irregular completed-action form.
Se leaves the discoverer unnamed, while han descubierto presents the discovery as completed and relevant now.
Agujeros is plural, de links the compound, and seguridad identifies the technical field in which the weaknesses exist.
Sistema names the thing, and the neutral descriptive adjective afectado follows it.
Although sistema ends in -a, it is masculine, so the matching singular adjective is afectado.

regions.labelEs: FEDORA CORE — VULNERABLE A CIERTO CIFRADO CÉSAR.

excludedUnits.rationale: Fedora Core is the unchanged proper name of a Linux distribution, not Spanish vocabulary.
César is the historical proper name retained inside the conventional cipher name, not a general Spanish vocabulary word.

applications.explanationEn: Vulnerable describes the system, a introduces the risk, and cierto cifrado names the particular cipher involved; the proper name remains visible but unscheduled.

regions.labelEs: XANDROS (EEE PC) — DA ACCESO ROOT SI SE LE PIDE CON VOZ FIRME.

excludedUnits.rationale: Xandros is the unchanged proper name of a Linux distribution, not Spanish vocabulary.
EEE PC is the unchanged commercial computer-model name in parentheses, not Spanish vocabulary.
Root is the unchanged Unix account label for the highest-privilege user, not a Spanish lexical word.

applications.explanationEn: Da is the present form of dar for the system, and acceso names what it grants.
Si introduces the possible condition, and pide remains an ordinary present-time form; se and le belong to the request construction between them.
Se leaves the requester unnamed, while pide supplies the present request action; le identifies the system receiving the request.
Voz names the thing, and the neutral descriptive adjective firme follows it.
Firme has one singular form for both genders, so it already matches the feminine singular noun voz.

excludedUnits.rationale: Gentoo is the unchanged proper name of a Linux distribution, not Spanish vocabulary.

applications.explanationEn: Vulnerable describes the system, a introduces the risk, and la adulación names that risk.

regions.labelEs: OLPC OS — VULNERABLE AL POWERBOOK DE JEFF GOLDBLUM.

excludedUnits.rationale: OLPC OS is the unchanged operating-system project label, not Spanish vocabulary.
PowerBook is the unchanged Apple product-family name, not Spanish vocabulary.
Jeff Goldblum is a person's proper name retained from the source joke, not Spanish vocabulary.

applications.exampleEs: VULNERABLE AL POWERBOOK DE JEFF GOLDBLUM
applications.explanationEn: Vulnerable takes al before the named device, and de marks the device's owner; the product and personal names remain visible but unscheduled.

applications.explanationEn: Si introduces the possible condition, and dice stays in the ordinary present form; the intervening words state its subject and content.
